General biased associative model (nests the uncfam family)

Source: R/model-uncfam_general.R
uncfam_general.Rd

A single biased associative model (Kachergis et al. 2012) whose extensions are free parameters, so that the package's uncfam() variants are nested special cases and can be compared by fitting one model with parameters fixed or freed. On each trial, a word-object pair \((w, o)\) on the trial receives a share of the trial's associative weight $$X_t \cdot \frac{b(w, o) + \epsilon s(w, o)}{1 + \epsilon \sum s}, \quad b(w, o) \propto M_{w,o}^{\gamma} e^{\lambda (U(w) + U(o))}$$ where \(U\) is each stimulus's uncertainty (entropy of its associations, or novelty), \(s\) is elimination support (see uncfam_elimination()), and \(X_t = X \cdot (\bar{H}_{trial} / \bar{H}_{all})^\kappa\) scales the trial's weight by its objects' relative uncertainty (see uncfam_attention()). With finite K, attention is sampled rather than allocated: each word attends to K objects drawn in proportion to \(b\), and only sampled pairs share the weight (see uncfam_sampling()); as K grows every pair is sampled and this approaches K = Inf.

Usage

uncfam_general(
  X,
  B,
  C,
  gamma = 1,
  eps = 0,
  kappa = 0,
  K = Inf,
  uncertainty = c("entropy", "novelty"),
  rho = 0,
  Cs = 0.5
)

Arguments

X

Associative weight to distribute

B

Weighting of uncertainty vs. familiarity (\(\lambda\))

C

Decay

gamma

Familiarity exponent (1 = uncfam())

eps

Weight of learning by elimination (0 = none)

kappa

Exponent on trial-level attention scaling (0 = none, 1 = uncfam_attention())

K

Objects sampled per word per trial (Inf = deterministic allocation; finite = sampled attention, a stochastic model)

uncertainty

Uncertainty measure: "entropy" (default) or "novelty" (1 / (1 + times seen))

rho

Weight of the short-term trace in familiarity (0 = none)

Cs

Per-trial decay of the short-term trace (used only if rho > 0)

Value

An object of class xslMod

Details

A short-term trace (rho > 0) adds recency to the familiarity bias: every update also goes into a second matrix \(S\) that decays by Cs per trial (vs. C for \(M\)), and familiarity in \(b\) becomes \((M + \rho S)^\gamma\), so a pairing strengthened on a recent trial draws extra attention. The trace affects only allocation during learning: uncertainty, elimination, and test performance use \(M\).

Special cases (each reproduces the named function exactly):

defaultsuncfam()
B = 0familiarity only
gamma = 0uncfam(variant = "uncertainty-only")
uncertainty = "novelty"uncfam(variant = "novelty")
gamma freeuncfam_gamma()
eps freeuncfam_elimination()
kappa = 1uncfam_attention()
K finiteuncfam_sampling()

uncfam_predictive() is not nested: its prediction-error update is unnormalized, a different class of rule.

Examples

dat <- get_example_ambiguous_condition()
xsl_run(uncfam_general(X = .1, B = .98, C = 1), dat)
#> $fits
#> $fits[[1]]
#> $fits[[1]]$sims
#> NULL
#> 
#> $fits[[1]]$responses
#>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3]      [,4]
#> [1,] 0.3888889 0.3888889 0.3888889 0.3888889
#> 
#> $fits[[1]]$perf
#>         1         2         3         4 
#> 0.3888889 0.3888889 0.3888889 0.3888889 
#> 
#> $fits[[1]]$matrix
#>       1     2     3     4
#> 1 0.035 0.035 0.010 0.010
#> 2 0.035 0.035 0.010 0.010
#> 3 0.010 0.010 0.035 0.035
#> 4 0.010 0.010 0.035 0.035
#> 
#> $fits[[1]]$sse
#> [1] 0.04938272
#> 
#> $fits[[1]]$data
#> xslData object with label "example condition" and condition "ambiguous"
#>   training trials: 2
#>       test trials: 0
#>             words: 4
#>           objects: 4
#>        accuracies: 4
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> $sse
#> [1] 0.04938272
#> 
#> $unweighted_sse
#> [1] 0.04938272
#> 

# nested comparison: does freeing gamma improve on uncfam()?
xsl_run(uncfam_general(X = .1, B = .98, C = 1, gamma = .5), dat)$sse
#> [1] 0.04938272

# sampled attention (stochastic)
xsl_run(uncfam_general(X = .1, B = .98, C = 1, K = 1), dat, control = xslControl(n_sim = 50))
